transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-14 09:00 PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Ortega, Samir P., Ava N., Tom B., Rosa K.
Link shared: https://redwood.example.com/poc/oc-bml-template (placeholder link)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping to align success criteria, workload sizing for a 6-week build-measure-learn POC focused on multilingual extraction and scoring of carbon-trading documents. Discussed shortlist of open models for quality vs cost tradeoffs and constraints for Private deployment/VPC. Agreed next steps for benchmark template and sample data.

Topics: success criteria, throughput & latency targets, model shortlist (open models), multilingual quality tradeoffs, security/compliance asks, timeline and next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. quick icebreaker — Lina are you in SF or Madrid?
[00:07] Dr. Lina Ortega: ah sorry, I'm in Madrid — good morning for me — thanks for doing this.
[00:12] Jordan: awesome, quick agenda, 1) success criteria 2) workload and sizing 3) model shortlist and tradeoffs 4) security / deployment constraints 5) next steps. sound ok?
[00:20] Samir (Platform): yes, that's perfect. we have the CTO joining part-way; we'll try to keep this tight.
[00:26] Priya (SE): great, I'll jump in with some questions around token profiles and concurrency so we can sketch a bench plan.
[00:33] Tom (CTO): hi — Tom here, sorry for joining a bit late.

[01:05] Dr. Lina: for success criteria we have three measurable goals: precision/recall on named-entity extraction for carbon project IDs and quantities (we want >= 88% F1 baseline), latency under 700ms p50 in the hosted mode for interactive review, and per-request cost target under $0.02 for typical 600-token request. also multilingual — spanish and portuguese matter most, french as secondary.
[01:35] Jordan: ok that helps — the F1 target is useful, and the cost window too. when you say 600 tokens is that prompt+response or just response?
[01:42] Ava: prompt+response, usually 450 token prompt with 150 token structured output.
[01:47] Priya: noted — so average around 600, tail maybe 1200 for long docs. what's your expected concurrency?
[01:55] Samir: baseline 20 concurrent users, peak 150 concurrent during end-of-day batch ingest where we also run automated scoring.
[02:05] Priya: ok that gives us throughput targets — we'll size for sustained throughput and also show a Dedicated pool scenario if needed.

[03:10] Jordan: on models — we propose a small shortlist of open models to test in the POC. initial candidates: Llama 3 8B (opt), OpenLLaMA-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a quantized Gemma-13B variant. we should test both full precision and 4-bit/8-bit quantizations for cost tradeoffs.
[03:33] Dr. Lina: would Mistral do better for the Spanish/Portuguese texts? we've seen Llama variants struggle on some Iberian legal phrasing.
[03:45] Priya: yeah there are known differences — smaller instruction-tuned models sometimes generalize poorly on non-English, so we'll include multilingual evaluation sets. also tokenizer mismatch matters — we may see token inflation for Portuguese in some tokenizers.
[04:05] Tom (CTO): what's the story for private deployment? we can't send PII out of our VPC for the pilot. we need either Redwood Private in our VPC or an on-prem package. is that possible in a POC?
[04:18] Jordan: yes, we can run Redwood Private — for POC we usually spin a scoped Private instance in your AWS account (VPC) with a small Dedicated GPU pool. can be done in the 6-week timeline if infra approvals are fast. sometimes legal/security needs an extra week for access.
[04:34] Rosa (Legal): what logs are captured? we need audit logs and the ability to disable usage analytics. SOC2 is a must, and we require KMS integration for key control.
[04:44] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest, and audit logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/CloudWatch. SOC 2 attestation and tooling pack are in our security packet — we'll include a redacted copy for review.

[05:30] Jordan: turning back to benchmarks — Priya, can you describe the bench template?
[05:35] Priya: sure — we'll run two primary experiments: 1) Latency SLO experiment: 1000 QPS synthetic ramp at 1–50 concurrency with KV cache off, then on. measure p50/p95/p99. 2) Quality sweep: run the 5 prompt sets across each model, compute entity extraction metrics (precision/recall/F1) and a human spot-check on 200 samples. cost calc: tokens * model pricing/throughput math for hosted vs dedicated. we'll also test quantized flavors and CPU fallbacks if GPU capacity scarce.
[06:10] Samir: for the ramp, is continuous batching going to change latency numbers?
[06:14] Priya: yes, continuous batching helps throughput but can increase p50 slightly; we'll capture both steady-state and cold-start behaviors. Redwood runtime has batching knobs — we'll report suggestions to hit your cost target without violating latency target.

[07:05] Dr. Lina: on quality, would you run instruction-tuning or prompt engineering first? we have internal templates we want to keep.
[07:12] Priya: we'll start with your prompts unchanged to get a baseline, then recommend few-shot or prefix tuning patterns. we can also try lightweight LoRA if you want model-level fine tuning — that's out of scope for the core POC but we can include as optional follow-up.
[07:30] Jordan: ok, timeline — 6 weeks 'build-measure-learn' divided: week 1 onboarding + infra; week 2 data ingest and baseline runs; weeks 3-4 bench sweeps and quality eval; week 5 iterate on prompts/config; week 6 wrap, recommendations and next-stage proposal.
[07:48] Samir: does that assume we give access to an AWS account? or can Redwood host?
[07:52] Jordan: both options. hosted is fastest (no infra approvals), private/VPC takes extra setup. for your PII constraint you flagged, VPC/private in your account is recommended.

[09:10] Dr. Lina: model shortlist question: you mentioned Gemma-13B, is that stable for production? I've seen variance in generation.
[09:18] Priya: Gemma family has strong performance on instruction tasks but we should validate variance and hallucination on domain-specific numbers — that's why the human spot checks are important. Also some open model weights vary between forks — we'll record exact checkpoints and seed settings.
[09:36] Ava: about quantization — if we go 4-bit for cost, what's the expected drop in extraction F1?
[09:41] Priya: depends on model; for some 13B models, 4-bit may see a 1–4 point delta in F1; for others negligible. we'll include a quantization sweep in the bench.

[10:20] Tom: SLA question — if we run dedicated pool, what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer for POC?
[10:25] Jordan: dedicated pools can be backed by a service-level commitment in enterprise contracts; for POC we demo typical p95/availability but formal SLA is in Reserved/Dedicated contracts. we'll outline expected latencies from our perf profiles.

[11:00] Samir: security again — can you sign our standard DPA?
[11:03] Jordan: yes, Redwood has a template DPA and we can start redlining; Priya will send security packet + SOC2 and support contacts.

[12:02] Dr. Lina: one more on metrics — we'd like drift detection on extraction confidence and a regression alert if F1 drops by >3 points vs baseline. can Redwood hook into our monitoring?
[12:12] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize can run quality monitoring; for POC we'll set up alerting to your webhook/Slack and include simple drift dashboards.

[13:00] Jordan: ok wrapping up — quick recap and owners. Jordan will send bench template, model shortlist, estimated cost buckets. Priya will prepare latency runbook and quantization matrix. Ava will upload sample prompts. Samir will provide concurrency profile and security contacts.
[13:25] Tom: timeline sounds good. we'll aim to approve infra request by Mon so you can start week 1 as planned.
[13:35] Rosa: legal will review DPA, expect comments within 3–4 business days.

[14:00] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run and share the docs.

Caveats / transcription noise:
- occasional mis-typed product names (Redwood Private sometimes logged as Redwood Privat).
- tokenizer and model names may be spelled differently in notes (Llama vs LLAMA etc).
- some attendee attribution for rapid back-and-forth may be approximate.

End of transcript.
